hook
A Big Mac is the same burger everywhere. Same bun, same patties, same sauce.
prices
So why does it cost about eight dollars in Switzerland, six in the US, and around two-forty in Taiwan?
beef
It's not the beef. It's everything around it.
wages
First: wages. A Swiss McDonald's worker earns several times more per hour than one in Taiwan, and that pay is baked into every burger.
rent
Second: rent. A restaurant in Zurich pays far more for its space than one in Taipei.
local
Third: local costs. Taxes, energy, and ingredients are all priced locally.
index
That's why economists love this burger. In 1986, The Economist created the Big Mac Index.
fx
The idea: if the same burger costs wildly different amounts, a currency may be overvalued, or undervalued.
caveat
But a cheap Big Mac can also just mean that life costs less there.
outro
So next time you travel, check the Big Mac price. And follow The Common Cents for more money, explained.
